src/screens/SearchScreen.tsx.whatsWrong: Default sort is by name (filters.sortBy defaults to 'name', L125), so `a.name.localeCompare(b.name)` runs in the filter effect on EVERY non-visual-search load for the full product list. mapProduct assigns `name: data.name` with NO default (confirmed L19 of productService), so a DB row with a null name yields product.name===null. `null.localeCompare(...)` throws (the receiver being null crashes; the argument being null is coerced to 'null' and is fine).
src/screens/SearchScreen.tsx.rootCause: Product.name is typed `string` but mapProduct does not defend against null DB data, and the sort assumes non-null.
src/screens/SearchScreen.tsx.failureScenario: Supabase returns any product row whose `name` column is null/missing (bad import, partially-created product). On screen open, loadProducts populates products, the filter effect sorts by name (default), hits `a.name.localeCompare(b.name)` with a.name===null, throws 'Cannot read properties of null (reading localeCompare)', crashing the search screen for ALL users until that row is fixed.
src/screens/SearchScreen.tsx.fix: Guard both operands: `? (a.name || '').localeCompare(b.name || '') : (b.name || '').localeCompare(a.name || '')`. (Ideally also default name in mapProduct.)

src/screens/SearchScreen.tsx.whatsWrong: loadProducts' catch only console.error's (L146); it sets no error state. On failure isLoading→false and products stays []. The skeleton (L632) only shows while isLoading, so after a failed load the user drops to the ListEmptyComponent which says 'No results / Clear filters' (L774-784). There is no retry, no pull-to-refresh (FlashList has no refreshing/onRefresh), and 'Clear filters' calls resetFilters which does NOT re-run loadProducts — so the user is stuck on a misleading empty screen with no way to recover without leaving and re-entering.
src/screens/SearchScreen.tsx.rootCause: Error is logged but not surfaced as state; no retry affordance and the empty state is indistinguishable from a genuine zero-result set.
src/screens/SearchScreen.tsx.failureScenario: User opens Search on a flaky/no connection. getProducts rejects, catch swallows it, screen shows 'No results found — try adjusting filters'. User taps 'Clear filters' (the only button), nothing reloads; they conclude the store is empty.
src/screens/SearchScreen.tsx.fix: Add `const [error, setError] = useState(false)`; in catch set setError(true) (clear it at start of loadProducts); render a distinct error view with a Retry button that calls loadProducts when error && products.length===0, and/or add `refreshing={isLoading} onRefresh={loadProducts}` to the FlashList.

src/screens/auth/ForgotPasswordScreen.ts.whatsWrong: handleContinue is an async submit handler whose only re-entrancy guard is the button's disabled={loading} prop. loading is React state, so the native view's disabled flag only flips a frame AFTER setLoading(true) commits and re-renders. A fast double-tap (two touch events dispatched to JS within ~1 frame, the exact 320dp low-RAM scenario) fires handleContinue twice while the button is still natively enabled. In the email branch this calls sendPasswordResetEmail(email) twice -> the user receives TWO reset emails and TWO stacked success Alerts; in the phone branch it fires two isPhoneRegistered network calls and can push VerifyPhone twice.
src/screens/auth/ForgotPasswordScreen.ts.rootCause: No synchronous in-flight guard; reliance on async state (loading) to gate a synchronous tap.
src/screens/auth/ForgotPasswordScreen.ts.failureScenario: Arabic user on a slow network double-taps 'Send Code' with a valid email. Both taps pass validation before the first render commits disabled=true, so sendPasswordResetEmail runs twice: two emails, two 'Password reset email sent' alerts to dismiss.
src/screens/auth/ForgotPasswordScreen.ts.fix: Add a synchronous ref guard. Import useRef, then: const inFlight = useRef(false); at the top of handleContinue add `if (inFlight.current) return; inFlight.current = true;`, and in the finally block add `inFlight.current = false;` alongside setLoading(false). (Also add an early `if (loading) return;` as belt-and-suspenders.)

src/screens/auth/ForgotPasswordScreen.ts.whatsWrong: const countryInfo = getCountryInfo(selectedCountry); then countryInfo.dialCode. getCountryInfo is typed to return CountryInfo (non-optional) but its body is `return countries[code]`, which is undefined for any code not in the map. selectedCountry is seeded from useUserRegion(), which does `setRegion(parsed.code as CountryCode)` — an unchecked cast of AsyncStorage JSON. If 'user_region' holds a legacy/corrupt/garbage code, countryInfo is undefined and countryInfo.dialCode throws a TypeError, crashing the phone-reset flow. TypeScript hides this because the return type lies.
src/screens/auth/ForgotPasswordScreen.ts.rootCause: getCountryInfo's declared return type omits undefined; the region value is cast, never validated.
src/screens/auth/ForgotPasswordScreen.ts.failureScenario: Legacy build stored {"code":"UK"} (not a valid ISO code; UK should be GB) in user_region. On this screen the user picks the Phone tab, enters a number, taps Send -> getCountryInfo('UK') is undefined -> `${countryInfo.dialCode}` throws -> screen crashes (caught only if wrapped, but this line is before any per-field guard and inside the try, so it surfaces as the generic 'Failed to process request' at best or an unhandled crash if error.message access also fails).
src/screens/auth/ForgotPasswordScreen.ts.fix: Guard it: const countryInfo = getCountryInfo(selectedCountry); if (!countryInfo) { setSelectedCountry('IQ'); Alert.alert(t('auth.error'), t('auth.errors.invalidCountry', { defaultValue: 'Please select a valid country' })); setLoading(false); return; } — or fall back: const countryInfo = getCountryInfo(selectedCountry) ?? getCountryInfo('IQ').

src/screens/auth/RegisterScreen.tsx.whatsWrong: handleContinue's phone branch does `const countryInfo = getCountryInfo(selectedCountry)` then reads `countryInfo.dialCode`. getCountryInfo (phoneUtils.ts line 435-437) returns `countries[code]` with NO fallback and is typed to return CountryInfo but actually returns `undefined` for any code not in the map. `selectedCountry` is seeded from `userRegion`, which useUserRegion produces via `parsed.code as CountryCode` (useUserRegion.ts line 21) — an unchecked cast of whatever JSON sits in AsyncStorage `user_region`. A legacy/garbage stored code (e.g. 'UK' instead of 'GB', a lowercase 'iq', or a full country name from an older build) is a valid string but absent from `countries`, so getCountryInfo returns undefined and `.dialCode` throws. Phone is the DEFAULT method (line 230), so this is the primary path.
src/screens/auth/RegisterScreen.tsx.rootCause: Unsafe `as CountryCode` cast on persisted data + getCountryInfo has no undefined guard (contrast getCountryFlag line 449-451 which uses `countries[code]?.flag || '...'`), and the screen dereferences the result immediately.
src/screens/auth/RegisterScreen.tsx.failureScenario: Device has a stale/corrupted `user_region` value like `{"code":"UK"}` in AsyncStorage (old build, migrated data). User opens Register (phone method), types a number, taps Continue → getCountryInfo('UK') returns undefined → `undefined.dialCode` → TypeError → red-screen/native crash on every Continue tap.
src/screens/auth/RegisterScreen.tsx.fix: Guard with a valid fallback: `const countryInfo = getCountryInfo(selectedCountry) || getCountryInfo('IQ');` (IQ is always present in the map, so `countryInfo.dialCode` on line 287 is then safe). Ideally also make getCountryInfo return `CountryInfo | undefined` so callers are forced to handle it.

src/screens/auth/RegisterScreen.tsx.whatsWrong: The Continue button relies solely on `disabled={isDisabled}` (isDisabled = loading) to prevent re-entry, but handleContinue itself has no in-flight guard. `disabled` is bound to state that is only committed on the next render; two taps dispatched in the same gesture frame (before React commits loading=true) both execute the full handler, since neither checks `loading` at entry.
src/screens/auth/RegisterScreen.tsx.rootCause: State-based disable has a sub-frame race; the async handler never short-circuits on an already-in-flight call.
src/screens/auth/RegisterScreen.tsx.failureScenario: Fast double-tap on Continue (common on 320dp low-RAM Android where the first render lags). In mock mode isPhoneRegistered resolves near-instantly, so both invocations pass the exists check and both call navigation.navigate('VerifyPhone', ...) → two VerifyPhone screens pushed on the stack (user must press back twice), plus a duplicate network/registration check.
src/screens/auth/RegisterScreen.tsx.fix: Add a guard at the very top of handleContinue: `if (loading) return;` (before line 275). A `useRef(false)` in-flight flag set/cleared around the async work is even more robust against the render-timing race.

src/screens/auth/RegisterSuccessScreen.t.whatsWrong: The auto-continue setTimeout (lines 82-84) is never captured and the useEffect returns no cleanup function (line 89). The 2s timer therefore keeps running after the component unmounts. Concrete failure: user taps 'Continue' at t=0.5s -> handleContinue() runs navigation.reset to 'Main' and this screen unmounts; the pending timer is still alive and at t=2s fires handleContinue() again, dispatching a SECOND navigation.reset({index:0}) onto the root. Anything the user did in the 1.5s after landing on Main (opened a product, scrolled into a category) is wiped by the delayed reset. Backgrounding the app mid-timer produces the same stray reset when it fires.
src/screens/auth/RegisterSuccessScreen.t.rootCause: setTimeout handle not stored; effect has no return () => clearTimeout(...).
src/screens/auth/RegisterSuccessScreen.t.failureScenario: Land on success screen -> tap Continue at 0.5s (reset to Main) -> navigate into a product on Main -> at 2s the un-cleared timer fires handleContinue() -> navigation.reset wipes the Main stack out from under the user.

src/screens/auth/RegisterSuccessScreen.t.whatsWrong: handleContinue() has no in-flight guard, so navigation.reset can be dispatched multiple times. Two concrete triggers: (a) the auto-timer AND a manual button tap both call it (even with the timer cleanup above, a tap that fires in the same frame the timer resolves races it), and (b) an impatient user double-taps 'Continue' (line 119-121) on a slow 320dp Android before the first reset re-renders, firing reset({index:0, routes:[Main]}) twice. Duplicate root resets can flash/rebuild the Main navigator twice and drop transient state.
src/screens/auth/RegisterSuccessScreen.t.rootCause: No hasNavigated ref/flag gating the single-shot navigation action.
src/screens/auth/RegisterSuccessScreen.t.failureScenario: User double-taps Continue quickly on a slow device -> handleContinue runs twice -> navigation.reset dispatched twice, rebuilding the Main tab navigator a second time.

src/screens/auth/SetNewPasswordScreen.ts.whatsWrong: The 'Not now' skip TouchableOpacity has no disabled={loading} prop and handleSkip has no in-flight guard, while the primary submit button IS disabled during loading. Both handlers call registerWithPhone + navigate.
src/screens/auth/SetNewPasswordScreen.ts.rootCause: Only the primary button was given a loading guard; the skip path was overlooked. setLoading(true) is async, so it cannot stop synchronous re-entry either.
src/screens/auth/SetNewPasswordScreen.ts.failureScenario: On slow Iraqi mobile network, user taps 'Create password' (handleSubmit sets loading=true, registerWithPhone in flight, primary button greys out). Impatient user taps 'Not now' -> handleSkip fires concurrently, calling registerWithPhone AGAIN with the same phone/name and then navigating to RegisterSuccess before the first request resolves. Two concurrent registration attempts + premature navigation. Separately, two fast taps on 'Not now' both enter handleSkip before the first setLoading re-renders, double-registering.
src/screens/auth/SetNewPasswordScreen.ts.fix:
Add disabled={loading} to the skip TouchableOpacity (line 385) and add an early guard `if (loading) return;` at the top of both handleSubmit and handleSkip. e.g.
<TouchableOpacity onPress={handleSkip} disabled={loading} style={[styles.quietButton, loading && { opacity: 0.5 }]} activeOpacity={0.6}>

src/screens/auth/SetNewPasswordScreen.ts.whatsWrong: handleSkip only registers when `mode === 'register' && method === 'phone' && name`. For an email registration (method === 'email'), it skips registration entirely yet still calls setRegistrationInProgress(false), refreshUser(), and navigate('RegisterSuccess').
src/screens/auth/SetNewPasswordScreen.ts.rootCause: The skip button visibility gate (line 383: isRegister && mode !== 'partner-register') shows the button for email-register, but handleSkip's guard excludes email, so it becomes a no-op-then-navigate.
src/screens/auth/SetNewPasswordScreen.ts.failureScenario: User picks email signup in AboutYouScreen (navigates here with mode:'register', method:'email'). On the password screen they tap 'Not now'. No account is created (email has no passwordless path), but they are sent to the RegisterSuccess screen as if registered. They later cannot sign in — a ghost account that never existed.
src/screens/auth/SetNewPasswordScreen.ts.fix: Hide skip for email register (change line 383 gate to `isRegister && mode !== 'partner-register' && method === 'phone'`), or in handleSkip block/branch email: if method === 'email' and no password was set, do not navigate to success — surface an error or require a password.

src/screens/auth/VerifyPhoneScreen.tsx.whatsWrong: For mode register/admin-register/partner-register the screen calls setRegistrationInProgress(true) at line 240 BEFORE verifying the code, but the catch block (285-289) that runs when verification fails only sets the error, clears the boxes and refocuses — it never resets the flag back to false. This flag is a module-level ref in AuthContext (registrationInProgressRef); while it is true, AuthContext's onAuthStateChanged handler (line 155-158) returns early on EVERY auth event and never calls setUser. So a failed OTP during registration permanently disables the global auth listener.
src/screens/auth/VerifyPhoneScreen.tsx.rootCause: The registration gate is opened on the optimistic (pre-verify) path but only ever closed by downstream success screens; the error path has no compensating reset.
src/screens/auth/VerifyPhoneScreen.tsx.failureScenario: Iraqi user picks Register, requests OTP, mistypes the 6-digit code (or SMS arrives late / network blips). AuthService.verifyPhoneCode throws, catch runs, registrationInProgress stays true. User gives up, taps 'Use a different phone/email' (line 507) -> SignIn, logs in with an existing email+password successfully. onAuthStateChanged fires with a real Supabase session, but line 155 sees the flag still true and returns early -> setUser is never called -> the app stays on the auth stack showing a logged-out UI despite a valid session. Only a full app restart recovers.

src/screens/messenger/ChatThreadScreen.t.whatsWrong: The keyboard effect animates translateY to -keyboardHeight on BOTH platforms, but Android is configured with windowSoftInputMode="adjustResize" (AndroidManifest.xml:42, app.json:48). Under adjustResize the OS already shrinks the window when the keyboard opens, so the position:absolute bottom:0 composer is ALREADY sitting exactly on top of the keyboard. The extra Animated translateY of -keyboardHeight (fired on keyboardDidShow, i.e. AFTER the resize) then lifts the composer a full keyboard-height ABOVE the keyboard, leaving a huge empty gap and floating the input box into the middle of the screen the instant the user starts typing.
src/screens/messenger/ChatThreadScreen.t.rootCause: Same manual keyboard-avoidance path applied to a platform that already does it natively via adjustResize.
src/screens/messenger/ChatThreadScreen.t.failureScenario: Android user taps the composer -> keyboard opens -> window resizes composer above keyboard -> keyboardDidShow fires -> composer jumps up ~300dp, detaching from the keyboard with a large blank gap; on a 320dp low-RAM phone the input can land behind the header. iOS is unaffected (iOS does not auto-resize, so the translate is needed there).
src/screens/messenger/ChatThreadScreen.t.fix: Skip the manual translate on Android: `useEffect(() => { if (Platform.OS === 'android') return; const onShow = (e:any) => Animated.timing(translateY,{toValue:-(e?.endCoordinates?.height??0),duration:240,useNativeDriver:true}).start(); const onHide = () => Animated.timing(translateY,{toValue:0,duration:220,useNativeDriver:true}).start(); const s = Keyboard.addListener('keyboardWillShow', onShow); const h = Keyboard.addListener('keyboardWillHide', onHide); return () => { s.remove(); h.remove(); }; }, [translateY]);` (leave translateY at 0 on Android; adjustResize positions the composer).

src/screens/messenger/ChatThreadScreen.t.whatsWrong: onSend clears the input with setText('') at line 132 BEFORE awaiting sendMessage, and the try block has a finally but NO catch. sendMessage (chatService.ts:398-401) re-throws on any failure. So on a thrown send the user's typed text is already gone, there is zero error UI, and because onSend is an async fn invoked from onPress without await, the rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection.
src/screens/messenger/ChatThreadScreen.t.rootCause: Optimistic clear with no rollback and no catch on a promise that rejects.
src/screens/messenger/ChatThreadScreen.t.failureScenario: On slow/no network, or when the seller has blocked the thread (chatService throws 'This conversation is blocked'), or 'Conversation not found': user types a long message, taps send, the field clears, the spinner flips back off — and the message silently vanishes with no toast/retry. The user believes it was sent. Plus a redbox in dev / unhandled-rejection log in prod.
src/screens/messenger/ChatThreadScreen.t.fix: Add a catch that restores the text and notifies: `try { await sendMessage(conversationId, trimmed, user.uid, 'user'); requestAnimationFrame(() => listRef.current?.scrollToOffset({ offset: 0, animated: true })); } catch (e) { setText((prev) => prev || trimmed); Alert.alert(t('chat.sendFailed', { defaultValue: 'Message failed to send. Tap send to retry.' })); } finally { setSending(false); }` (import Alert from react-native).

src/screens/messenger/ChatThreadScreen.t.whatsWrong: The in-flight guard uses the `sending` state value captured in the render-time closure, and `disabled` (line 300) is likewise driven by render-time state. Neither updates until React commits the setSending(true) re-render. Two fast taps landing in the same frame both execute the same onSend closure where `sending===false` and `text===trimmed`, so both call sendMessage and a duplicate message is inserted.
src/screens/messenger/ChatThreadScreen.t.rootCause: State-based guard is asynchronous; it does not block re-entry within the same frame.
src/screens/messenger/ChatThreadScreen.t.failureScenario: On a 320dp low-RAM Android device where a render can lag several frames, an impatient double-tap on Send posts the same message twice to the conversation.
src/screens/messenger/ChatThreadScreen.t.fix: Add a synchronous ref guard: `const sendingRef = useRef(false);` then in onSend `if (!trimmed || sendingRef.current || !user?.uid) return; sendingRef.current = true; setSending(true); ...` and in finally `sendingRef.current = false; setSending(false);`.

src/screens/messenger/ConversationsScree.whatsWrong: When user?.uid becomes falsy (logout, or switch to guest), the effect early-returns after setLoading(false)/setRefreshing(false) but never clears `items`. The subscription callback is the ONLY writer of `items`, and it does not fire in the logged-out branch, so the previous account's full conversation list (store names + last-message text) stays in state and on screen.
src/screens/messenger/ConversationsScree.rootCause: The `!user?.uid` guard handles the spinner but omits resetting list state; because this screen is guest-aware (isGuest/LoginGate on line 610) it stays mounted across auth transitions rather than being unmounted, so stale state persists.
src/screens/messenger/ConversationsScree.failureScenario: User A signs in, opens Messenger (loads 12 private supplier chats), signs out to guest. AuthContext.user goes null, the effect re-runs, unsubscribes, and returns without clearing items. User A's private conversations and last messages remain fully visible to whoever now holds the device (guest / next user) until a new subscription overwrites them.

src/screens/profile/ChangePasswordScreen.whatsWrong: handleResendOTP only guards on `if (cooldown > 0) return`, and the button is `disabled={cooldown > 0}` — neither checks `loading`. When cooldown hits 0 the button becomes enabled, and `setCooldown(30)` only runs AFTER `await sendOTP(...)` resolves, so for the entire network round-trip cooldown stays 0 and the button stays enabled.
src/screens/profile/ChangePasswordScreen.rootCause: The in-flight state (`loading`) is not part of the guard/disabled condition; the cooldown that would block re-taps is set only after the awaited request completes.
src/screens/profile/ChangePasswordScreen.failureScenario: On the OTP screen the 30s cooldown expires. User taps 'Resend code'; nothing visibly changes for ~1-2s on a slow Iraqi mobile connection, so they tap it again. Both taps pass `cooldown > 0 === false`, firing two `sendOTP(userPhone)` calls → two real SMS sent (telco cost) and `verificationId` overwritten twice; the code from the first SMS may no longer match the stored verificationId, confusing the user.
src/screens/profile/ChangePasswordScreen.fix: Guard on loading in both places: `const handleResendOTP = async () => { if (cooldown > 0 || loading) return; ... }` and `<TouchableOpacity onPress={handleResendOTP} disabled={cooldown > 0 || loading} ...>`.

src/screens/profile/ChangePasswordScreen.whatsWrong: The 'Forgot password?' link and the phone/email method cards fire `handleSendPhoneOTP` / `handleSendEmailReset`, which set `loading=true` inside their try block. The only guard is `disabled={loading}`, which relies on a React re-render to take effect.
src/screens/profile/ChangePasswordScreen.rootCause: No synchronous in-flight ref; the guard becomes effective only after the loading state flushes to the UI, leaving a window where two queued touch events both dispatch.
src/screens/profile/ChangePasswordScreen.failureScenario: On a low-RAM 320dp Android with a laggy JS thread, two rapid taps on the phone method card queue before React flushes the first `setLoading(true)`. Both invocations of `handleSendPhoneOTP` run, sending two OTP SMS (or two password-reset emails), each a real billable side effect.
src/screens/profile/ChangePasswordScreen.fix: Add a synchronous guard, e.g. `const inFlight = useRef(false);` at the top of each network handler: `if (inFlight.current) return; inFlight.current = true; try { ... } finally { inFlight.current = false; setLoading(false); }`. Do the same in the primary change/set/verify handlers for defense in depth.

src/screens/profile/MyAddressScreen.tsx.whatsWrong: The map block is gated only by a truthy check `address.coordinates &&` (line 297). `coordinates` comes straight from a Supabase jsonb column with NO validation (addressService.mapDbToAddress: `coordinates: data.coordinates`). The overlay at line 365 then calls `address.coordinates.latitude.toFixed(6)` and `.longitude.toFixed(6)` directly. If the DB row holds a truthy-but-partial/garbage object — `{}`, `{latitude: 33}`, `{latitude: null, longitude: null}` (partial save, migration artifact, or manual/garbage data) — the truthy check passes and `.toFixed` is called on `undefined`/`null`, throwing 'Cannot read property toFixed of undefined' during render. This throws for the WHOLE screen (every card re-renders), so one bad address blanks the entire address list via ErrorBoundary, not just its own card.
src/screens/profile/MyAddressScreen.tsx.rootCause: Truthy object check instead of numeric-field validation; unvalidated jsonb passthrough in the service.
src/screens/profile/MyAddressScreen.tsx.failureScenario: A user has an address whose jsonb `coordinates` was saved as `{latitude: 33.31}` (longitude missing) or `{}`. On opening My Addresses, line 297 truthy-check passes, line 365 evaluates `.longitude.toFixed(6)` on undefined -> TypeError thrown in render -> entire MyAddressScreen crashes to the error boundary; user cannot see or manage ANY of their addresses.
src/screens/profile/MyAddressScreen.tsx.fix: Guard on the actual numeric fields, both at the map condition (line 297) and the no-coordinates condition (line 373). Add a helper: `const hasCoords = (a: Address) => typeof a.coordinates?.latitude === 'number' && !isNaN(a.coordinates.latitude) && typeof a.coordinates?.longitude === 'number' && !isNaN(a.coordinates.longitude);` then use `{hasCoords(address) && (` at 297 and `{!hasCoords(address) && (` at 373. (SafeMapView already does this internally for iOS at its line 72; the screen's own overlay at 365 does not.)

src/screens/profile/MyAddressScreen.tsx.whatsWrong: `loadAddresses` unconditionally calls `setLoading(true)` on line 58, and `if (loading)` (line 420) returns a FULL-SCREEN centered spinner that replaces the entire list+ScrollView+RefreshControl. Because `loadAddresses` runs on every `useFocusEffect` (line 78) and inside `onRefresh` (line 71): (a) every time the user returns to this screen (e.g. after AddEditAddress) the already-rendered list is torn down and flashes the full-screen loader; (b) pull-to-refresh is visibly broken — as soon as the fetch starts, `loading` flips true, the ScrollView (and thus the RefreshControl spinner the user is looking at) is unmounted and replaced by the full-screen loader, so the pull-to-refresh spinner vanishes mid-gesture.
src/screens/profile/MyAddressScreen.tsx.rootCause: Single `loading` flag reused for initial load, focus-refetch, and pull-to-refresh; full-screen loading branch not distinguished from background refresh.
src/screens/profile/MyAddressScreen.tsx.failureScenario: User pulls to refresh: the RefreshControl spinner appears, then instantly the whole list disappears and a centered 'Loading' spinner takes over, then the list pops back. Also: user taps a saved address to edit, hits back — instead of seeing their list, the screen blanks to a full-screen spinner every single time.
src/screens/profile/MyAddressScreen.tsx.fix: Only show the full-screen loader on the very first load. E.g. gate line 58 with `if (addresses.length === 0 && !refreshing) setLoading(true);` (and keep the `finally` setLoading(false)). This keeps the list mounted during focus-refetch and pull-to-refresh so the RefreshControl handles its own spinner.

src/screens/profile/PaymentMethodsScreen.whatsWrong: loadExchangerInfo only ever CALLS setSavedExchangerInfo when data exists (line 95-97); it never resets it to null. The `!user?.uid` early-return (line 84-86) also fails to clear it. The mount effect re-runs on `[user?.uid]` change. So when the auth user changes to null (logout / session expiry / token-refresh failure while the screen stays mounted) or switches from a user WHO HAS saved info to one who has NONE, savedExchangerInfo retains the previous user's private financial data — exchange office name/phone and receiver name/phone — and keeps rendering it in the 'Saved Money Exchanger' card (lines 464-563).
src/screens/profile/PaymentMethodsScreen.rootCause: Load function treats 'no data' as 'do nothing' instead of 'clear', so stale per-user state survives an account change.
src/screens/profile/PaymentMethodsScreen.failureScenario: User A saves exchanger info (receiver name + phone). Session expires and AuthContext sets user to null (screen still mounted); effect re-runs, hits `!user?.uid`, returns without clearing. User B logs in with no saved info; loadExchangerInfo fetches null, so the `if (data?.money_exchanger_info)` guard is false and setSavedExchangerInfo is never called — User B now sees User A's receiver name and phone number auto-filling at checkout.

src/screens/profile/PaymentMethodsScreen.whatsWrong: money_exchanger_info is a free-form JSONB column cast blindly with `as SavedMoneyExchangerInfo` (line 96). The saved-card maps its fields directly into <Text> children (lines 499-503 -> 517). If any stored field is an object or array (corruption, a different writer, or a schema change), `<Text>{item.value}</Text>` throws React's 'Objects are not valid as a React child' and the screen crashes on render.
src/screens/profile/PaymentMethodsScreen.rootCause: `as` cast asserts a shape the DB does not guarantee for a JSONB column.
src/screens/profile/PaymentMethodsScreen.failureScenario: A row where money_exchanger_info was written as `{ officeName: { name: 'X' }, ... }` (or an admin/import script stored a nested object). On open, savedExchangerInfo is truthy, the saved card renders, and line 517 tries to render the object child -> hard crash, no error boundary recovery for this screen's content.
src/screens/profile/PaymentMethodsScreen.fix: Coerce/validate after fetch. Minimal: render `value: typeof savedExchangerInfo.officeName === 'string' ? savedExchangerInfo.officeName : String(savedExchangerInfo.officeName ?? '')` (repeat per field), or normalize once in loadExchangerInfo by mapping each field through String()/'' and dropping non-object shapes. Stop trusting the raw JSONB via `as`.

src/screens/profile/UpdatePhoneScreen.ts.whatsWrong: handleVerify has no in-flight guard. It is auto-invoked the moment the 6th digit is entered (L142 paste path, L150 single-digit path). During the network round-trip loading=true disables the Confirm button (L320) but NOT the OTP TextInputs, which also have selectTextOnFocus (L310). A nervous/fast user tapping a filled box selects its digit; typing replaces it, fires handleOTPChange, all-6-filled is still true, and handleVerify runs a SECOND time with the same token. The second supabase.auth.verifyOtp for type 'phone_change' fails (token already consumed), lands in catch, matches /invalid|expired|token|otp/, sets 'Incorrect or expired code.' and clears the code array (L198) — even though the FIRST call already succeeded and is about to update the profile. The user sees a false error over a successful verification.
src/screens/profile/UpdatePhoneScreen.ts.rootCause: Async submit handler with no re-entrancy guard, plus OTP inputs left interactive during loading.
src/screens/profile/UpdatePhoneScreen.ts.failureScenario: User types the 6th digit → auto-verify starts (slow network) → user impatiently taps a box and re-types a digit → second verifyOtp fires, fails on the reused token → 'Incorrect or expired code.' flashes and all boxes clear, contradicting the success Alert that may also appear.
src/screens/profile/UpdatePhoneScreen.ts.fix: Add `if (loading) return;` as the first line of handleVerify (and handleResend, L205, which is likewise unguarded and only gated by cooldown). Optionally add `editable={!loading}` to the OTP TextInputs (L298) so they can't be retriggered while a verify is in flight.

src/screens/profile/UpdatePhoneScreen.ts.whatsWrong: After supabase.auth.verifyOtp succeeds (L177-178) the phone is already changed and verified on the Supabase auth user, but updateUserProfile (L181) and refreshUser (L182) are awaited afterward with no separation. If either throws (flaky network, RLS hiccup on public.users), control jumps to the catch block which shows a generic/'already in use'/'incorrect code' error AND clears the code array (L198). The user believes the whole operation failed and will re-enter or resend — but the OTP was already consumed, so verify/resend behave inconsistently, and auth.phone is now out of sync with public.users.phone (the row the app actually reads).
src/screens/profile/UpdatePhoneScreen.ts.rootCause: Auth-side change and app-side mirror are in the same try; a failure in the mirror step is reported as a total failure with no compensation or distinct messaging.
src/screens/profile/UpdatePhoneScreen.ts.failureScenario: verifyOtp succeeds, then refreshUser() fails on a dropped connection → user sees 'Something went wrong. Please try again.', code clears, they tap Resend → new SMS but the number is already changed at auth → confusing loop, and the app's users row still shows the old number.
src/screens/profile/UpdatePhoneScreen.ts.fix: Separate the two phases: after a successful verifyOtp, wrap the mirror in its own try/catch that does NOT clear the code or claim the code was wrong — e.g. still show the success Alert but log/queue a retry of updateUserProfile/refreshUser, or show a distinct 'Phone verified — finishing sync…' message. Only the verifyOtp failure path should reset the code.

src/screens/store/StoreCompanyTab.tsx.whatsWrong: The Location card, its initialRegion, and openMap all gate only on `profile.location` being truthy — they never verify latitude/longitude are finite numbers. `mapDbToProfile` assigns `location: data.location` with zero validation, so a DB row with `location: {}` or a partial `{latitude: 33.3}` (missing longitude) flows straight through as a truthy object. SafeMapView guards coordinates internally ONLY on iOS (`hasCoords = lat != null && !isNaN(lat)`); on Android it forwards `initialRegion={{ latitude: undefined, longitude: undefined, ... }}` directly to the native react-native-maps MapView.
src/screens/store/StoreCompanyTab.tsx.rootCause: Truthiness check on an object instead of validating its numeric fields; Android path in SafeMapView has no coordinate guard.
src/screens/store/StoreCompanyTab.tsx.failureScenario: Server returns a store whose `location` JSON is present but incomplete (e.g. `{}` or only a latitude). On a 320dp Android device the native MapView receives undefined/NaN coordinates in initialRegion -> map renders blank / at 0,0 or emits a native error; tapping 'Open in Maps' or 'Directions' builds `geo:undefined,undefined` / `maps:undefined,undefined` which never resolves.
src/screens/store/StoreCompanyTab.tsx.fix: Compute a validated flag once and use it everywhere: `const hasGeo = profile.location && Number.isFinite(profile.location.latitude) && Number.isFinite(profile.location.longitude);` then render the card with `{hasGeo && (...)}` and early-return in `openMap` unless `hasGeo`.

src/screens/store/StoreCompanyTab.tsx.whatsWrong: `openMap` calls `Linking.openURL(url || '')` with NO `.catch()`, unlike the sibling `openUrl` helper (line 61) which correctly swallows rejections. `Platform.select` only defines ios/android, and the iOS scheme `maps:${lat},${lng}` (no `//?ll=`) is malformed. Any of: no maps app installed (Android), unsupported scheme, or an empty/undefined url causes openURL to reject with no handler.
src/screens/store/StoreCompanyTab.tsx.rootCause: Missing .catch on a Linking.openURL promise and a non-standard iOS URL scheme.
src/screens/store/StoreCompanyTab.tsx.failureScenario: User on an Android phone with no geo-capable app (or iOS where `maps:33.3,44.4` isn't recognized) taps 'Directions' / 'Open in Maps'. openURL's promise rejects unhandled -> dev red-box 'Possible unhandled promise rejection', and in production the button silently does nothing with no user feedback.
src/screens/store/StoreCompanyTab.tsx.fix: Mirror `openUrl`: `Linking.openURL(url || '').catch(() => {});` and use a valid iOS URL, e.g. `ios: \`https://maps.apple.com/?ll=${lat},${lng}\``.

src/screens/CategoryProductsScreen.tsx.whatsWrong: The catch block (L60-62) swallows every fetch error and just sets products to []. There is no distinct error state — a network/server failure renders the exact same 'No products available' empty view (L155-162) as a genuinely empty category, with no retry button. On a slow/no-network Iraqi device, getProductsByCategory throws, the user sees 'No products available', concludes the category is truly empty, and leaves — when the data merely failed to load. The only recovery (pull-to-refresh) is unsignposted.
src/screens/CategoryProductsScreen.tsx.rootCause: Error and empty are conflated into one state (products.length === 0); no error flag is tracked and no retry affordance is rendered.
src/screens/CategoryProductsScreen.tsx.failureScenario: User on subway (no network) taps a category tile. getProductsByCategory() rejects -> catch sets products=[] -> screen shows 'No products available'. User believes the category is empty and never learns it was a network error.
src/screens/CategoryProductsScreen.tsx.fix: Add `const [error, setError] = useState(false);`. In load(): `setError(false)` at the start of try, and in catch do `setProducts([]); setError(true);`. Then branch ListEmptyComponent (or the container) on `error` to show a distinct message + a retry TouchableOpacity that calls `load()`, e.g. `{error ? <ErrorRetry onRetry={load}/> : <EmptyState/>}`.

src/screens/ChatScreen.tsx.whatsWrong: The recording timer interval (recordingTimerRef, created at 1709) is only cleared inside cancelRecording (1729) and stopAndSendRecording (1743). There is no unmount cleanup: the isRecording effect at 1326 only returns `pulse.stop()` and no other effect clears the timer or stops audioRecorder. If the user starts a voice recording then navigates back (component unmounts) or the screen is popped, the setInterval keeps firing setRecordingDuration on an unmounted component forever and audioRecorder.record() keeps the mic hot / file open.
src/screens/ChatScreen.tsx.rootCause: Missing component-unmount cleanup for recordingTimerRef and audioRecorder.
src/screens/ChatScreen.tsx.failureScenario: User taps mic to record a voice message, then taps the back arrow (or a deep-link navigates away) mid-recording. The 1s interval leaks and keeps calling setState indefinitely; the microphone/recorder is never stopped, so the mic indicator stays on and the temp audio file is never released. Repeat a few times on a 320dp low-RAM Android and you accumulate live intervals + orphaned recorders.
src/screens/ChatScreen.tsx.fix: Add an unmount-only effect: `useEffect(() => () => { if (recordingTimerRef.current) clearInterval(recordingTimerRef.current); audioRecorder?.stop?.().catch(() => {}); isRecordingIntentRef.current = false; }, []);`

src/screens/ChatScreen.tsx.whatsWrong: The preview-modal send button (TouchableOpacity at 2664) has no disabled/in-flight guard, and handleSendPreviewImage's early `if (!previewUri) return` (1527) does not protect against a synchronous double-invocation: setPreviewUri(null)/setPreviewVisible(false) are async, so two taps in the same frame both read the still-set previewUri and each run a full upload + sendMessage.
src/screens/ChatScreen.tsx.rootCause: No synchronous in-flight guard on the image-send path (unlike onSend which guards on `sending`).
src/screens/ChatScreen.tsx.failureScenario: On a slow network the send button stays on screen for a moment; an impatient user double-taps it. Both taps pass the previewUri check before React flushes the null, producing two uploads of the same image and two duplicate image messages in the thread (and two optimistic bubbles).
src/screens/ChatScreen.tsx.fix: Guard synchronously with a ref or state: at the top of handleSendPreviewImage add `if (!previewUri || sendingPreviewRef.current) return; sendingPreviewRef.current = true;` and reset it in a finally block; optionally also set `disabled={sendingPreviewRef.current}` on the button.

src/screens/NotificationsScreen.tsx.whatsWrong: The realtime-subscription effect lists selectedFilter and showOnlyUnread in its dependency array. Every filter-tab tap and unread-toggle therefore tears down the Supabase channel (cleanup at line 104) and builds a brand-new one, and NotificationService.subscribeToNotifications internally issues a FORCED network fetch (getUserNotifications(true), service line 292) on every re-subscribe. Worse, the old subscription's in-flight `getUserNotifications(true).then(callback)` can still resolve AFTER its channel was removed and invoke the OLD callback, which runs setNotifications + filterNotifications(data, OLD selectedFilter, OLD showOnlyUnread) — overwriting the list handleFilterChange just set with the NEW filter.
src/screens/NotificationsScreen.tsx.rootCause: Filter values are captured into the subscription closure via deps to avoid a stale closure, but that couples subscription lifecycle to filter state and reruns the forced refetch.
src/screens/NotificationsScreen.tsx.failureScenario: On a slow Iraqi 2G connection the user taps All -> Orders -> Promos -> System. Four channel teardown/creates and four forced refetches fire. The 'Orders' refetch resolves after the 'System' tap and applies the stale 'order' filter, so the list flashes the wrong subset before settling. Repeated rapid tapping also spams the network and flickers the list.
src/screens/NotificationsScreen.tsx.fix: Subscribe once. Keep filter values in refs and read them inside the callback: `const filterRef = useRef({selectedFilter, showOnlyUnread}); useEffect(()=>{filterRef.current={selectedFilter,showOnlyUnread};});` then in the effect use `[filterNotifications]` deps only and call `filterNotifications(updated, filterRef.current.selectedFilter, filterRef.current.showOnlyUnread)`. This keeps one channel for the screen's life and re-filters cheaply on the client.

src/screens/auth/LegacyEmailLoginScreen..whatsWrong: handleLogin has no in-flight guard at its top; it validates and then awaits loginWithEmail. The only protection is `disabled={loading}` on the button, but setLoading(true) is asynchronous, so a fast double-tap can fire onPress twice before the disabled re-render commits, issuing two concurrent loginWithEmail() calls and stacking two 'Welcome back' Alerts.
src/screens/auth/LegacyEmailLoginScreen..rootCause: Guard relies on async React state (disabled={loading}) that has not committed yet when the second synchronous onPress fires; there is no synchronous re-entrancy check.
src/screens/auth/LegacyEmailLoginScreen..failureScenario: On a slow low-RAM Android the re-render after setLoading(true) is delayed tens of ms; a user impatiently double-taps Login, both taps pass validation and both call AuthService.signInWithIdentifier concurrently — two auth requests race, the second can overwrite the session, and two success Alerts stack on screen.
src/screens/auth/LegacyEmailLoginScreen..fix: Add a synchronous re-entrancy guard as the first line of handleLogin: `if (loading) return;` (place it before the validation block so the second tap short-circuits immediately, independent of the async disabled prop).

src/screens/auth/OnboardingScreen.tsx.whatsWrong: The <ScrollView> (line 51) has NO `flex: 1` (only `contentContainerStyle`). In a React Native flex column (SafeAreaView flex:1 with the footer as a sibling), the ScrollView's default flexBasis is `auto`, so its own frame collapses to its CONTENT height instead of filling the available space. Two consequences: (1) the intended vertical centering never happens — `contentContainerStyle.justifyContent:'center'` (line 104) has no extra space to center within, so on a tall/large screen the hero content clusters near the top and the footer/CTA floats mid-screen instead of pinned to the bottom; (2) because the ScrollView is sized to its content, it is NOT height-constrained and therefore CANNOT scroll when content exceeds the viewport.
src/screens/auth/OnboardingScreen.tsx.rootCause: ScrollView is given contentContainerStyle but no `style={{flex:1}}`/`flex:1`, so it is not bounded by its parent and collapses to intrinsic content height; `flexGrow:1` on the content container only affects the inner content view, not the ScrollView's outer frame.
src/screens/auth/OnboardingScreen.tsx.failureScenario: 320dp low-RAM Android at max OS font size with Arabic/Kurdish (which wraps the 3 bullet points onto more lines): logo(88) + margins + title(28pt, multi-line) + subtitle + three wrapped points exceed the short viewport. The ScrollView grows to that content height and pushes the footer (the ONLY 'Get Started' button — the sole exit from this full-screen zIndex:9998 overlay) below the screen edge. Since the ScrollView isn't height-constrained it does not scroll, so the user cannot reach 'Get Started' and is trapped on onboarding with no way into the app.
src/screens/auth/OnboardingScreen.tsx.fix: Constrain the ScrollView's height so it fills the parent and becomes scrollable: add a style. Change `<ScrollView contentContainerStyle={styles.content} ...>` to `<ScrollView style={styles.scroll} contentContainerStyle={styles.content} ...>` and add `scroll: { flex: 1 }` to the StyleSheet. This pins the footer to the bottom, makes the `justifyContent:'center'` centering actually work, and lets tall content scroll so the CTA is always reachable.

src/screens/profile/AddEditAddressScreen.whatsWrong: handleSave has no synchronous in-flight guard. The only protection against a second invocation is the Button's `disabled={loading}` (Button.tsx l190), which is driven by async React state — it only takes effect after setLoading(true) causes a re-render. A rage-tap / very fast double-tap (and the isDefault checkbox row at l1223 is a second, separately-tappable trigger path only for that field, not this) can pass the `if (!user?.uid) return` and reach addressService.addAddress twice.
src/screens/profile/AddEditAddressScreen.rootCause: Guard relies on async `loading` state instead of a synchronous ref; addAddress has no idempotency key.
src/screens/profile/AddEditAddressScreen.failureScenario: On a 320dp low-RAM Android under GC pause, user taps 'Add Address' twice within one frame before the re-render disables the button. addressService.addAddress runs twice; it is not idempotent (INSERT with no dedupe, addressService.ts l100-104). Both calls also independently compute isFirstAddress→isDefault=true (addressService l72-81), so the user gets TWO identical addresses, both flagged default.
src/screens/profile/AddEditAddressScreen.fix: Add a ref guard at the top of handleSave: `const savingRef = React.useRef(false); ... if (savingRef.current) return; savingRef.current = true;` and reset it in the finally block (`savingRef.current = false;`) alongside setLoading(false).

src/screens/profile/AddEditAddressScreen.whatsWrong: The mount effect's loadDefaults() does a functional setFormData that carefully preserves user input with `prev.x || default` for every field EXCEPT coordinates (l240: `coordinates: resolvedCoordinates`), which is written unconditionally and with no isMounted/latest-write check. Its own resolvedCoordinates comes from a getCurrentPositionAsync(Balanced) started at l169 that can resolve seconds later, racing handleGetCurrentLocation (l403, High accuracy).
src/screens/profile/AddEditAddressScreen.rootCause: Unconditional overwrite inside an otherwise merge-preserving async update, with no cancellation or 'already set' guard.
src/screens/profile/AddEditAddressScreen.failureScenario: New-address screen opens with location permission already granted → loadDefaults starts a slow Balanced GPS fix. The user immediately taps the prominent 'Use current location' button (handleGetCurrentLocation), which resolves first and sets precise High-accuracy coordinates. The still-pending loadDefaults fix then resolves and its setFormData at l240 overwrites the user's coordinates with the older/less-accurate Balanced fix (out-of-order write). If loadDefaults had NO permission, resolvedCoordinates is undefined and l240 can wipe coordinates the user just set back to undefined.
src/screens/profile/AddEditAddressScreen.fix: Guard coordinates like the other fields: `coordinates: prev.coordinates || resolvedCoordinates,` (and/or bail out of loadDefaults' setFormData if isMountedRef.current is false).

src/screens/profile/EditProfileScreen.ts.whatsWrong: `new Date(user.createdAt).getFullYear()` is rendered with no validity check. In this hybrid Firebase/Supabase app `user` is `any` and createdAt's shape is unverified. A Firestore Timestamp object ({seconds,nanoseconds}) or malformed string produces Invalid Date -> getFullYear() = NaN, rendering 'Member since NaN'. If createdAt is Unix seconds (e.g. 1700000000) instead of ms, `new Date(seconds)` is interpreted as ms since epoch -> 'Member since 1970'. Either way the user sees a wrong/garbage year.
src/screens/profile/EditProfileScreen.ts.rootCause: Unguarded Date construction on untyped API data plus ambiguous seconds-vs-ms units.
src/screens/profile/EditProfileScreen.ts.failureScenario: Backend returns createdAt as a Firebase Timestamp object or seconds-based number; the profile hero shows 'Member since NaN' / 'Member since 1970'.
src/screens/profile/EditProfileScreen.ts.fix: Guard for validity before rendering: `{(() => { const d = user?.createdAt ? new Date(user.createdAt) : null; if (!d || isNaN(d.getTime())) return null; return (<Text allowFontScaling={false} style={{ fontSize: 13, color: labelColor, marginTop: 4 }}>{t('profile.memberSince', { defaultValue: 'Member since {{year}}', year: d.getFullYear() })}</Text>); })()}` — and normalize the unit upstream (multiply seconds by 1000, or unwrap Timestamp) so the year is correct.

src/screens/profile/HelpSupportScreen.ts.whatsWrong: The screen's single support CTA ('Chat on WhatsApp') calls openWhatsApp(BRAND.contactPhone, ...), but BRAND.contactPhone is the hardcoded placeholder 'TODO_CONTACT_PHONE' (config.ts:7, no env override). openWhatsApp strips non-digits to '' and opens whatsapp://send?phone=&text=... (and wa.me/?text=... fallback) with NO recipient. openWhatsApp's trailing .catch(()=>{}) swallows every failure, so the button gives zero feedback. There is no guard against an empty/invalid phone before firing.
src/screens/profile/HelpSupportScreen.ts.rootCause: Config placeholder (documented 'until finalized') combined with the screen offering no fallback or guard when the number is not a real phone.
src/screens/profile/HelpSupportScreen.ts.failureScenario: User with an unanswered question taps the only support button. WhatsApp opens to a blank 'no contact' state (or wa.me shows an invalid-number error), then nothing. They believe the app is broken and cannot reach support. Even after launch, if contactPhone is ever misconfigured/empty, the button silently no-ops.
src/screens/profile/HelpSupportScreen.ts.fix: Guard before opening and give feedback, e.g.: `const phone = BRAND.contactPhone.replace(/\D/g, ''); if (!phone) { Alert.alert(t('helpSupport.title'), t('helpSupport.contactUnavailable', { defaultValue: 'Support contact is not available yet.' })); return; } openWhatsApp(phone, t(...));` — and/or hide the button when no real number is configured. (Also replace the placeholder in config.ts before release.)

src/screens/profile/UpdateEmailScreen.ts.whatsWrong: handleDone has no in-flight guard and the Done TouchableOpacity (L153) has no disabled prop. handleDone awaits reloadUser() (a supabase.auth.getUser() network round-trip). A user who double-taps Done on a slow/low-RAM device fires handleDone twice; both invocations eventually call navigation.goBack(), popping TWO screens instead of one (e.g. skipping the Profile screen straight back to Home).
src/screens/profile/UpdateEmailScreen.ts.rootCause: Async handler triggered by a button with no disabled/loading guard, and goBack() is not idempotent when dispatched twice before the transition settles.
src/screens/profile/UpdateEmailScreen.ts.failureScenario: On 3G, user taps 'Done' on the success screen; the reloadUser() await takes ~1s; during that second the user taps 'Done' again out of impatience. Two goBack() dispatches fire and the navigator pops past the intended parent screen, dumping the user an extra level back.
src/screens/profile/UpdateEmailScreen.ts.fix: Guard the handler and disable the button, e.g.: `const handleDone = async () => { if (loading) return; setLoading(true); await reloadUser(); refreshUser(); navigation.goBack(); };` and on the button `disabled={loading}` (or use a `useRef(false)` in-flight flag if you don't want the button to visually change).

src/screens/store/StoreProductsTab.tsx.whatsWrong: The 'New' filter does `filtered = [...filtered].reverse()` as a proxy for recency. The products array arrives NEWEST-FIRST from the service (getProductsByTenantId orders `.order('created_at', { ascending: false })`, productService.ts:349), and that same order is what 'All' renders. Reversing a newest-first list produces OLDEST-first, so tapping 'New' surfaces the store's oldest inventory — the exact opposite of the chip's meaning.
src/screens/store/StoreProductsTab.tsx.rootCause: reverse() assumes the source array is oldest-first, but the backend returns newest-first.
src/screens/store/StoreProductsTab.tsx.failureScenario: Admin adds a brand-new product today; store is on Supabase. Customer taps the 'New' chip expecting newest arrivals and instead sees the oldest products in the catalog first; the new item lands at the very bottom.
src/screens/store/StoreProductsTab.tsx.fix: Data is already newest-first, so drop the reverse. Either remove the branch entirely, or sort explicitly by date: `} else if (activeFilter === 'New') { filtered = [...filtered].sort((a, b) => new Date(b.createdAt as any).getTime() - new Date(a.createdAt as any).getTime()); }` — note createdAt is a raw ISO string from Supabase (mapProduct sets `createdAt: data.created_at`) despite the Timestamp type, so `.toMillis()` would throw; use `new Date(...)`.
